about: The priest offers the host to God the Father for his own sins, offences, and negligences, for all who are present, and for all faithful Christians, living and dead. He asks that the offering may avail both him and them unto salvation and eternal life.

s01.narrative: At Solemn Mass the deacon hands the celebrant the paten with the Host. At a private Mass the priest takes it himself and offers it while saying the prayer.

s02.translation: Receive, holy Father, almighty eternal God, this spotless Host, which I, Thy unworthy servant, offer to Thee, my living and true God, for my innumerable sins, offences and negligences, and for all here present, and also for all faithful Christians living and dead: that it may profit me and them unto salvation, into life everlasting. Amen.

w004.function: The vocative of a 3rd declension adjective is identical with the nominative. The address to the Father settles it.

w006.function: “Pater” (w003) and “Deus” are vocative together with their modifying adjectives.

w007.function: It agrees with “hóstiam” (w009) and points to the Host on the paten.

w010.function: A relative in the accusative because it is the object of “óffero” (w015). It takes gender and number from “hóstiam” (w009).

w011.function: An expressed subject pronoun, modified by “indígnus” (w012) and “fámulus” (w013).

w015.function: The verb of the relative clause beginning with “quam” (w010).

w021.function: The phrase “Deo vivo et vero” also occurs in 1 Thessalonians 1:9.

w024.function: The form is dative as well as ablative. The preposition “pro” (w022), which governs the ablative, decides.

w028.function: It denotes what was neglected or left undone.

w029.function: Ablative plural, sharing its case with all three preceding nouns.

w033.function: A participle used as a noun: “those standing around”, meaning those present.

w035.function: In the phrase “sed et”, it expands the list: “and also”.

w039.function: Both adjectives stand as nouns here: the faithful Christian people.

w042.function: A participle used as a noun: “the deceased”.

w044.function: Dative of advantage with “profíciat” (w047): to whom it is to be of profit.

w047.function: Subjunctive after “ut” (w043). Its subject is the offering previously named “hóstiam” (w009).
